name: Spider Solitaire
intro: A short path through Spider Solitaire: building down, moving same-suit runs and dealing, then why building in suit and emptying columns win games.

units.name: How Spider works
units.blurb: Building down, moving runs and dealing.

lessons.title: Building and moving runs
lessons.summary: In Spider you build down in any suit, but only same-suit runs move together. Learn the moves, the deal and how runs are cleared.
lessons.wrap: Any suit to build, one suit to move. Next: a quick rules check.

steps.text:
Spider has ten columns. Only the top cards are face up; the rest turn over as you clear the cards above them. The deck waits to deal more rows.

The goal is to build complete runs from King down to Ace in one suit. Each one is cleared away. Clear eight to win. The lessons show just part of a game, with two suits.
You can move a card onto any card one rank higher, in any suit.
steps.wrong: The 7♥ goes on an 8 of either suit.
steps.done: And the face-down card under it turns over.

steps.text: A run that is in order and all one suit moves as a block.
steps.wrong: Drag the 9♥, and the 8♥ comes with it.

steps.text: Now look at the 8♠ with the 7♥ on it.
steps.explain: No. Only same-suit runs move as a block. You’d have to move the 7♥ first.

steps.prompt: When you’re stuck, you deal a new row: one card on every column. What do you need first?
options: At least one card in every column
steps.explain: Every column needs at least one card before you deal.

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Four questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the strategy.

lessons.title: Spider rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Spider Solitaire rules: building down in any suit, moving same-suit runs, empty columns, dealing and completing a run.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the strategy.

steps.explain: Yes. Any suit will do when you build.

options: A run in order and all one suit

steps.prompt: What can go into an empty column?
steps.explain: Anything. That’s why an empty column is so useful.

steps.prompt: What happens when you complete King down to Ace in one suit?
steps.explain: It’s cleared. Clear eight runs to win.

lessons.title: Build in suit
lessons.summary: In Spider, a card on its own suit can move with it later; a card on another suit can’t. Learn to choose same-suit moves and uncover cards.
lessons.wrap: In suit when you can, and uncover cards when you can. Next: empty columns.

steps.text:
A 7♥ on an 8♥ can later move with it. A 7♥ on an 8♠ can’t: it makes a joint that has to be untangled later.

When two moves are possible, choose the one in suit.

steps.prompt: Move the 6♥ onto the 7 that keeps it in suit.
steps.wrong: Look for the 7 of the same suit as the 6♥.
steps.done: In suit, and it turned over a card too.

steps.text: Two in-suit moves: the 8♠ onto the 9♠, or the 10♥ onto the J♥. Only one of them turns a face-down card over.
steps.prompt: Make the in-suit move that uncovers a card.
steps.wrong: Of the 8♠ and the 10♥, which one is sitting on a face-down card?
steps.done: Every face-down card you turn over is new information and new options.

lessons.title: Empty columns
lessons.summary: An empty column is the most powerful thing in Spider. Learn to win one, why Kings need one, and why you shouldn’t waste it on a low card.
lessons.wrap: Win empty columns and spend them well. Make your useful moves before you deal. You’re ready to play.

steps.text:
An empty column can take any card or same-suit run. It lets you park cards, untangle mixed runs and rebuild in suit.

Columns with the fewest cards are the quickest to empty.
One column here holds a single card.
Nothing can go on top of a King in another column, so a King can only move into an empty column. The K♠ Q♠ here is sitting on face-down cards.
steps.prompt: Move the K♠ Q♠ into the empty column.
steps.wrong: Move the King and its Queen into the empty column.
steps.done: A King at the top of a column is perfect: you can build down from it where it stands, and you turned over a card.

steps.prompt: Should you drop a single low card into an empty column?
steps.explain: An empty column is worth more empty. Fill it with a King, or with a card that frees something useful.
